summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, chronic kidney disease, and diabetes was admitted for acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease, with a creatinine of 3.3, likely due to dehydration from poor oral intake related to excessive daytime fatigue. She reported ongoing somnolence, which impaired her ability to eat and drink regularly. IV fluids improved her kidney function, with creatinine decreasing to 2.0. The fatigue was attributed to sedating medications, particularly topiramate, which was tapered over two weeks, and citalopram was increased to 20 mg daily to improve alertness. Tacrolimus dose was increased due to a low trough level, and mycophenolate was restarted. Lower extremity edema persisted but imaging ruled out deep vein thrombosis. Home health services were arranged to support medication management and follow-up. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans for nephrology, cardiology, and transplant hepatology follow-up.
